title: Kingdom of Lithuania
capsule: This entry records Lithuania during the interwar period (1919–1940), when it functioned as an independent democratic and later authoritarian republic — formally styled the Republic of Lithuania — despite the Wikidata label 'Kingdom of Lithuania' reflecting a brief monarchical project of December 1918 that was dissolved before a king was ever crowned. The state was established following the collapse of German occupation at the end of World War I; Antanas Smetona led an authoritarian government from 1926 onward. Lithuania recovered the Memel Territory from France in 1923 but lost the Vilnius region to Poland in 1920, making Kaunas its provisional capital. The Soviet Union occupied and annexed Lithuania in June 1940 under the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of interwar Lithuania is well attested from League of Nations records and international treaties, though the contested status of the Vilnius region introduced a persistent boundary ambiguity in the northeast.
